name: Unauthorised Data Access
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Occurs when data is accessed by individuals or systems without proper authorisation, either externally (hackers) or internally (employees).
assessment_prompt: Can your data be accessed by individuals or systems without proper authorisation, whether external attackers or internal staff who shouldn't have access?

name: Unprotected Data Storage
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Refers to storage of data without adequate security measures such as encryption, access controls, or secure cloud configurations.
assessment_prompt: Is any of your data stored without adequate security measures such as encryption, access controls, or secure cloud configuration?

name: Unverified Data Sources
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Using datasets from unknown or unreliable sources that may contain sensitive, inaccurate, or illegal data.
assessment_prompt: Do you use datasets from unknown or unreliable sources that might contain sensitive, inaccurate, or illegal data?

name: Data Retention Failures
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Storing personal or sensitive data longer than necessary, increasing exposure to potential breaches.
assessment_prompt: Do you retain personal or sensitive data for longer than necessary, increasing exposure to potential breaches?

name: Insufficient Anonymisation
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Attempts to anonymise data fail, leaving information that can still identify individuals.
assessment_prompt: Could your anonymisation methods fail, leaving data that can still identify individuals?

name: Membership Inference Attacks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Attackers attempt to determine whether specific data records were used in training an AI model.
assessment_prompt: Could an attacker determine whether a specific person's data record was used to train your model?

name: Model Inversion Attacks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Reconstructing sensitive or private data from model outputs or predictions.
assessment_prompt: Could someone reconstruct sensitive or private data from your model's outputs or predictions?

name: Training Data Memorisation
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: AI models unintentionally "remember" exact sensitive information from the training dataset in their outputs.
assessment_prompt: Could your AI model unintentionally "remember" and reveal exact sensitive information from its training data in its outputs?

name: Prompt Injection / Output Manipulation
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Malicious inputs designed to make AI reveal hidden or confidential information.
assessment_prompt: Could a malicious input be crafted to make your AI reveal hidden or confidential information?

name: Adversarial Querying
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Systematic attempts to extract private or sensitive information by exploiting model behaviour.
assessment_prompt: Could someone systematically query your model to extract private or sensitive information by exploiting its behaviour?

name: API Exploitation
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Unauthorised use or abuse of AI system endpoints, which can expose data or functionality.
assessment_prompt: Could your AI system's API endpoints be misused or abused in ways that expose data or functionality?

name: Network Vulnerabilities
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Weaknesses in networks (e.g., unpatched servers, open ports, insecure protocols) that can be exploited to access data.
assessment_prompt: Are there weaknesses in your network (e.g. unpatched servers, open ports, insecure protocols) that could be exploited to access data?

name: Supply Chain Compromise
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Introduction of malicious or vulnerable components from third-party software, libraries, or pre-trained models.
assessment_prompt: Could malicious or vulnerable components enter your system via third-party software, libraries, or pre-trained models?

name: Configuration Errors
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Insecure default settings or misconfigurations in AI platforms that expose data or functionality.
assessment_prompt: Could insecure default settings or misconfigurations in your AI platform expose data or functionality?

name: Logging/Telemetry Leaks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Recording sensitive information in logs or telemetry without proper safeguards or redaction.
assessment_prompt: Do your logs or telemetry record sensitive information without proper safeguards or redaction?

name: Malicious Insider Actions
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Intentional actions by internal personnel to steal, expose, or misuse sensitive data.
assessment_prompt: Could an internal person intentionally steal, expose, or misuse sensitive data?

name: Human Error
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Accidental mistakes by individuals, such as sending data to wrong recipients or mismanaging sensitive files.
assessment_prompt: Could accidental mistakes by staff, such as sending data to the wrong recipient or mismanaging sensitive files, expose data?
note: Single most cited risk factor across the whole taxonomy.

name: Privilege Mismanagement
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Excessive or inappropriate access rights granted to employees or contractors, increasing the risk of misuse.
assessment_prompt: Do employees or contractors have excessive or inappropriate access rights that increase the risk of misuse?

name: Training/Operational Negligence
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), Privacy in the Age of AI: A Taxonomy of Data Risks
definition: Lack of awareness, training, or adherence to policies, resulting in unintentional data exposure.
assessment_prompt: Could a lack of awareness, training, or adherence to policy result in unintentional data exposure?

name: AI Governance & Privacy Compliance Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks associated with the alignment of AI governance frameworks with privacy compliance standards, leading to inadequate privacy protections.
assessment_prompt: Are your AI governance frameworks properly aligned with privacy compliance standards, or could gaps lead to inadequate privacy protections?

name: Evolving Regulatory Compliance Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks arising from changing regulatory requirements that may leave an organisation non-compliant with new laws or privacy standards.
assessment_prompt: Could changing regulatory requirements leave your organisation non- compliant with new laws or privacy standards?

name: Cross-Border Compliance & Data Sovereignty
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks related to non-compliance with varying data protection laws across different countries, impacting international data flow and sovereignty.
assessment_prompt: Could non-compliance with varying data protection laws across countries affect your international data flows or data sovereignty obligations?

name: Regulatory Uncertainty in AI-Quantum Systems
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from unclear or inconsistent regulations surrounding the integration of AI with quantum systems, potentially leading to privacy lapses.
assessment_prompt: Are there unclear or inconsistent regulations around integrating AI with quantum systems that could lead to privacy lapses for your system?

name: Emerging Technology Privacy Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks related to the privacy and security implications of rapidly evolving technologies — especially AI and quantum systems — including the lack of mature standards, ethical uncertainty, and risks from novel data processing capabilities.
assessment_prompt: Does your system use rapidly evolving technologies, especially AI or quantum, that lack mature standards, creating ethical uncertainty or novel data-processing risks?

name: Sensitive Data Exposure in Training Models
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks of privacy breaches and security vulnerabilities due to exposure of personal or sensitive data during AI model training, including memorisation, leakage via outputs, or weak training data protections.
assessment_prompt: Could personal or sensitive data be exposed during model training, via memorisation, output leakage, or weak training-data protections?

name: Post-Quantum Cryptography Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks associated with the security and privacy limitations of current cryptographic methods in the face of quantum computing, and uncertainties around post-quantum cryptographic algorithm adoption, implementation, and resilience.
assessment_prompt: Could your current cryptographic methods be vulnerable to quantum computing, or is there uncertainty about your post-quantum cryptography adoption or implementation?

name: Emerging AI Threats & Data Vulnerabilities
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Threats from the use or misuse of AI that introduce new attack surfaces or amplify privacy risks, such as adversarial inputs, model inversion, data poisoning, and unauthorised inference.
assessment_prompt: Could new AI-related attack surfaces, such as adversarial inputs, model inversion, data poisoning, or unauthorised inference, amplify privacy risk for your system?

name: Weak Access Controls & Data Security Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks stemming from inadequate security measures, such as weak authentication, insufficient authorisation, or poor encryption, leading to unauthorised access or exposure of private data.
assessment_prompt: Are there weak authentication, insufficient authorisation, or poor encryption practices that could lead to unauthorised access to private data?

name: AI Privacy Control Implementation Gaps
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Gaps in the design or enforcement of privacy-related controls (e.g., anonymisation, data minimisation, consent tracking) within AI workflows, which create both privacy vulnerabilities and potential security loopholes.
assessment_prompt: Are there gaps in how privacy controls, such as anonymisation, data minimisation, or consent tracking, are designed or enforced in your AI workflows?

name: Technical Privacy Control Gaps
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Shortcomings in technical safeguards meant to enforce privacy — such as differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, or secure federated learning — which can also weaken system security if poorly implemented or misconfigured.
assessment_prompt: Are technical privacy safeguards, such as differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, or secure federated learning, missing, weak, or poorly implemented in your system?

name: Privacy Safeguard Deficiencies in AI
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from insufficient or poorly integrated privacy protection mechanisms in AI systems, including both organisational policy gaps and technical safeguards, potentially compromising both user privacy and system security.
assessment_prompt: Are privacy protection mechanisms, whether policy or technical, insufficiently integrated into your AI system, risking both privacy and security?

name: Transparency & User Rights Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from insufficient transparency about how user data is handled, leading to violations of user rights.
assessment_prompt: Is there insufficient transparency about how user data is handled, which could lead to violations of user rights?

name: Bias & Fairness in AI Privacy
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from AI systems that introduce bias or unfairness in data handling, impacting user privacy.
assessment_prompt: Could bias or unfairness in your AI system's data handling impact user privacy?

name: User Consent & Control Mechanisms
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from inadequate mechanisms for users to give informed consent and control how their data is used.
assessment_prompt: Are your mechanisms for obtaining informed user consent and letting users control their data adequate?
note: Consolidated: the source table also lists a near-identical row "User Consent & Control Risks" (Count: 38; 5.32%) which was judged a duplication artefact and merged into this item rather than kept as a separate risk — dropping tool-list count for Paper B from 22 to 21 (kept for auditability, not deleted from the record; see MERGE_LOG.md).

name: Informed Consent Deficiencies
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from inadequate processes for obtaining informed consent, potentially violating privacy rights.
assessment_prompt: Could inadequate informed-consent processes potentially violate user privacy rights?

name: Loss of User Control Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from users losing control over their personal data when interacting with AI systems.
assessment_prompt: Could users lose control over their personal data when interacting with your AI system?

name: Compliance Monitoring Gaps
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks due to insufficient monitoring of compliance with privacy regulations, leading to potential violations.
assessment_prompt: Is your monitoring of privacy-regulation compliance insufficient, risking undetected violations?

name: Ongoing AI Auditing & Bias Mitigation
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from lack of continuous auditing and bias mitigation in AI systems that could compromise privacy.
assessment_prompt: Does your system lack continuous auditing and bias-mitigation processes that could otherwise catch privacy issues?

name: Monitoring Evolving AI Privacy Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from inadequate monitoring of new and emerging AI privacy threats, creating vulnerabilities.
assessment_prompt: Is your monitoring of new and emerging AI privacy threats inadequate, leaving vulnerabilities undetected?

name: Failure to Adapt to Emerging Risks
source_citation: Billiris, Gill & Bandara (2025), A Taxonomy of Data Risks in AI and Quantum Computing (QAI) — A Systematic Review
definition: Risks from the inability to detect and respond to new privacy threats from emerging AI technologies.
assessment_prompt: Would your organisation struggle to detect and respond to new privacy threats from emerging AI technologies?
